questions: With 16 mm footprints, does the outer pair (±0.04) respond smoothly across the tape edge, or do neighbouring footprints overlap so much that the signal saturates near centre?
Does the lighter 0.5 kg, 0.10 m track robot show more steering_oscillation than the baseline, and does control_effort rise with it?
Does the robot now leave the tape at a specific bend type (sharp slalom turns versus the s-bend), and does that point to the array width or to turn authority?
Is the sensor noise large compared with the near-centre signal now that the footprints are bigger?

intent: Revised geometry: five sensors at 2 cm spacing across ±4 cm, 4 cm ahead of the axle, with 16 mm footprints so the outer sensors respond sooner and the signal is graded across the array. Body reduced to 0.5 kg with a 0.10 m wheel track to lower yaw inertia and raise turn response. Goal: stop the uniform off-track exits seen in iteration 0 (max_error pinned at 0.061 m) and complete at least the oval or s-bend. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m, line_loss_events at or near zero, and completion on at least one development track.
learning: Iteration 0 showed a uniform off-track failure at 0.061 m on every track, with rms_error about 0.03. The next race tests whether faster yaw response and a sharper outer-sensor response stop the single excursion. If max_error is still pinned at 0.06 with low line loss, the cause is turn authority rather than sensing, and the next step is a wider array or a shorter wheel track. If line_loss_events rise, the 16 mm footprints are probably overlapping too much and the next step is to narrow them back to 12 mm and widen the spacing.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the baseline and every trial on all three development tracks ended off-track. Mean progress was 0.03 to 0.12, and max_error sat at about 0.061 m on every track. That is the off-track limit of 0.06 m, so the robot leaves the tape at the first real bend. Each run also logged one line-loss event, so the line was lost once and not recovered. rms_error was about 0.03 on all tracks, so the robot tracks reasonably until a single excursion takes it off. The integrator reports that with 12 mm footprints the outer sensors only respond once the line moves about 1 cm off centre, which gives a weak signal near centre and forces large outer weights. Changing the footprint to 16 mm makes the outer sensors respond sooner. A 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.02 overlaps the tape edge once the line centre is within about 0.5 mm of the sensor, and the x = ±0.04 sensors respond once the line moves about 2 cm. Overlapping footprints also make the signal more graded across the array. I am also reducing the wheel track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m and the mass from 0.7 kg to 0.5 kg. Both lower yaw inertia, mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, and a narrower track gives more turn rate per unit of wheel difference, so the robot should correct a drift faster before it reaches 6 cm. The off-track limit cannot be widened much with body_width, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + W/4) stays at 0.06 for any W up to about 0.19 m. The sensor row stays at y = 0.04 so the forward reaction distance does not change. Expected result: fewer off-track exits, at least one track completed, and max_error below 0.06. Several things change at once, so attribution will be rough, but the baseline is failing uniformly and a bolder move is justified.
